jobs.title: Assistant
jobs.description:
Qualification: Graduation from a recognized university.
Experience: No prior professional experience required.
IT Training: Selected candidates shall undergo 6 weeks of basic IT training, including Microsoft Office, conducted by NITB during the probation period.
Recruitment Process: Recruitment shall be conducted at district level in Balochistan with the assistance of newly established employment cells.
Selection Method: Walk in interview only. No entry test or written examination.
Domicile Requirement: Candidates must possess a valid Balochistan domicile.
Application Procedure: Eligible candidates shall apply online through the National Job Portal at www.njp.gov.pk within 15 days of publication of the advertisement.
Important Instructions:
Government employees must apply through proper channel.
Female candidates and persons with disabilities are encouraged to apply.
Incomplete applications and applications received after the closing date shall not be entertained.
The Establishment Division reserves the right to cancel, reduce or increase the number of vacancies at any stage.
No travelling allowance or daily allowance shall be admissible for the interview.
Contact: Establishment Division, Cabinet Secretariat, Islamabad
Telephone: 0519209372

jobs.title: Chief Software Architect
jobs.description:
Role purpose
The Chief Software Architect will provide strategic leadership for PDA’s software architecture and engineering direction, supporting the delivery of secure, scalable and interoperable digital platforms and government services. The role will translate the National Digital Masterplan and institutional requirements into software architecture standards, reusable capabilities and modernisation roadmaps.
Combining a strong software development background with executive leadership, the Chief Software Architect will guide critical technology decisions, strengthen engineering capability and oversee architectural quality across PDA-supported programmes.
Key responsibilities
Define and lead PDA’s software architecture strategy, aligning technology decisions with national digital priorities, service needs and delivery outcomes.
Establish reference architectures, software design standards and reusable patterns that support interoperability and consistent implementation across government programmes.
Lead application modernisation strategy, assessing legacy systems and defining practical roadmaps for migration, integration, replacement or retirement.
Guide the adoption of cloud-native architectures, APIs, microservices and other technologies where they meet business, operational and sustainability requirements.
Establish architecture governance and design assurance, working with the Architecture Review Board and relevant technology leaders to review major designs, resolve exceptions and manage technical debt.
Ensure software solutions address security, privacy, accessibility, resilience, performance and maintainability from design through operation.
Partner with DPI, data, AI, cybersecurity, product and delivery leaders to align software architecture with shared platforms and end-to-end service requirements.
Evaluate major technology investments and supplier proposals, considering technical suitability, lifecycle costs, portability, vendor dependency and knowledge transfer.
Strengthen software engineering practices, including secure development, automated testing, DevSecOps, release assurance and operational readiness.
Build and mentor architecture and engineering capability, providing technical direction to internal teams and delivery partners.
Advise the Chairperson and senior leadership on software strategy, emerging technologies, delivery risks and significant architectural decisions.
Qualifications and experience
Bachelor’s in Computer Science, Software

jobs.title: Chief Data Officer
jobs.description:
Role Purpose
Lead the development and institutionalisation of the National Data Strategy and data governance capabilities supporting secure, responsible and effective use of data. Build practical stewardship arrangements across institutions, recognising the continuing control and responsibilities of designated data custodians.
Key responsibilities
Lead the National Data Strategy and related governance frameworks, translating priorities into implementable policies, standards and adoption plans.
Define data ownership and stewardship arrangements, classification, quality, metadata, lineage, retention and lifecycle standards, with clear responsibilities and assurance measures.
Coordinate with ministries, provinces, regulators and data custodians to enable secure data sharing and resolve barriers to interoperability and adoption.
Work with DPI and Technology leaders on data exchange requirements, reference architectures and shared registries; retain focus on governance and stewardship responsibilities.
Develop proposals for open data, controlled access, sensitive data handling and cross-border arrangements with Legal, Security and relevant authorities, subject to applicable requirements and approvals.
Work in partnership with the AI Office on data readiness, provenance, quality and appropriate use of datasets supporting AI systems.
Build the Data governance team and institutional capability; establish maturity assessments, adoption measures and reporting on data quality and governance risks.
Education
Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Public Policy or a related discipline. A relevant master’s degree is preferred. Qualifications must meet PDA’s applicable recognition and equivalence requirements.
Essential experience
At least 15 years of progressively responsible relevant professional experience in data governance, architecture, strategy or transformation, including senior leadership responsibility.
Evidence of establishing and embedding data governance across multiple business units, institutions or jurisdictions, with measurable improvements in data quality, sharing or use.
Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and advising executive decision-makers on data policy, investment, privacy and operational trade-offs.
Desirable experience
Leadership of complex data governance or data transformation engagements in consulting, professional services or technology advisory is desirable. Equivalent leadership in p

jobs.title: Chief Product Officer
jobs.description:
Role Purpose
Lead the strategy, prioritisation and performance of the digital product portfolio assigned to PDA. Build a product management capability that converts policy priorities and citizen needs into secure, accessible services, working with responsible government service owners and PDA’s design, technology and delivery functions.
Key responsibilities
Develop the assigned product portfolio strategy and investment priorities in alignment with the National Digital Masterplan, public value and available delivery capacity.
Lead product discovery, business cases, roadmaps and lifecycle decisions from initial concept through launch, improvement and retirement, within approved decision rights.
Establish product outcomes and measures covering adoption, task completion, service quality, accessibility, reliability and cost-effectiveness; use evidence to guide investment.
Build and lead the product management team, defining decision rights and coaching product leaders in discovery, prioritisation and outcome accountability.
Partner with the Citizen Experience function to translate journey research and service design standards into product priorities, acceptance criteria and improvements.
Work with Technology, DPI, Data, AI and Security leaders to address feasibility, interoperability, privacy, resilience and reuse of shared capabilities.
Coordinate with ministries, service owners and Delivery Excellence on dependencies, operational readiness and benefits realisation; ensure learning continues after launch.
Education
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Product or Service Design, Engineering, Business Administration or a related discipline. A relevant master’s degree is preferred. Qualifications must meet PDA’s applicable recognition and equivalence requirements.
Essential experience
At least 15 years of progressively responsible relevant professional experience in digital product management or closely related product leadership, including senior leadership responsibility.
At least five years leading and developing product management teams, with accountability for a portfolio of complex digital products.
Evidence of managing live products through discovery, launch and sustained improvement, with measurable adoption, service or business outcomes.
Experience making portfolio trade-offs and managing product investment, stakeholder priorities and cross-functional delivery.
Desirable experience
Experience in GovTech, public services or compl

jobs.title: Chief AI Officer
jobs.description:
Role Purpose
Lead PDA’s AI governance capability and strategy for responsible adoption of AI in public services. Connect policy, technical assurance and applied use cases so that AI initiatives deliver measurable benefits with proportionate safeguards and effective human accountability.
Key responsibilities
Develop risk-based AI governance proposals, standards and assurance processes within PDA’s assigned remit, coordinating with Legal and relevant regulators.
Define approaches to impact assessment, transparency, fairness, explainability, human oversight and monitoring throughout the AI lifecycle.
Build and prioritise the government AI use-case portfolio with service owners, assessing public value, feasibility, data readiness, cost and risks before recommending investment.
Guide applied AI initiatives from evaluation and pilots through deployment and monitoring, working with Technology, Data, Product and Delivery Excellence.
Establish evaluation requirements for AI models and suppliers, including generative AI, covering performance, safety, security, privacy and operational suitability.
Advise on national AI capability, compute and model strategy, procurement requirements and ecosystem partnerships, subject to approved policy and investment decisions.
Build the AI team and institutional capability; coordinate readiness assessments, knowledge transfer and executive reporting on outcomes and risks.
Education
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Engineering, Technology Policy or a related discipline. A relevant master’s degree is preferred. Qualifications must meet PDA’s applicable recognition and equivalence requirements.
Essential experience
At least 15 years of progressively responsible relevant professional experience across AI, machine learning, technology strategy or technology policy, including senior leadership responsibility.
Demonstrated leadership of AI strategy or governance and sufficient technical depth to assess applied AI systems, deployment risks and assurance evidence.
Evidence of leading multidisciplinary teams and influencing executive stakeholders on responsible AI investment and adoption.
Experience taking complex technology initiatives into implementation with measurable outcomes and ongoing governance.
Desirable experience
Leadership of AI strategy, governance or transformation engagements in consulting, professional services or technology advisory is desirable. Comparable leadership in governme

jobs.title: Chief Strategy Officer
jobs.description:
Role Purpose
Lead the development, alignment and periodic refresh of the National Digital Masterplan and its strategic frameworks. Translate national priorities into evidence-based choices, coordinated sectoral plans and measurable outcomes, working across government, industry and PDA’s executive functions.
Key responsibilities
Lead formulation and refresh of the National Digital Masterplan and coordinate the supporting sectoral and implementation plans through the applicable governance and approval process.
Conduct strategic diagnostics and digital maturity assessments to identify capability gaps, dependencies and opportunities across sectors and institutions.
Develop policy and investment options supported by economic analysis, delivery feasibility, public value and clear prioritisation criteria.
Coordinate federal, provincial and local stakeholders, regulators and industry partners to align priorities, responsibilities and implementation commitments.
Lead strategic foresight and research, assessing emerging technologies and economic trends and translating findings into practical recommendations.
Define the strategic monitoring and evaluation framework, baselines and outcome measures; work with Delivery Excellence to distinguish implementation progress from realised impact.
Build strategy and research capability, brief executive and governance forums, and recommend course corrections when evidence or national priorities change.
Education
Bachelor’s degree in Public Policy, Economics, Business Administration, Technology Management, Engineering or a related discipline. A relevant master’s degree is preferred. Qualifications must meet PDA’s applicable recognition and equivalence requirements.
Essential experience
At least 15 years of progressively responsible relevant professional experience in strategy, public policy, digital transformation or economic planning, including senior leadership responsibility.
Evidence of developing and supporting implementation of national, sectoral or large organisational transformation strategies with measurable outcomes.
Experience in economic or business-case analysis, strategic prioritisation and negotiation across complex institutional stakeholders.
Demonstrated understanding of digital technologies and their implications for public services, institutions and economic development.
Desirable experience
Leadership of strategy and transformation engagements in consulting, professional services or technology advisory is desi

jobs.title: Chief Citizen Experience Officer
jobs.description:
Role Purpose
Lead PDA’s citizen experience strategy and oversight of end-to-end public service journeys. Establish a practical approach to understanding citizen needs, redesigning services across institutions and measuring whether services become easier, more inclusive and more effective.
Key responsibilities
Develop the National Citizen Experience Strategy and a life-event approach to priority journeys, such as starting a business or accessing family services.
Work with responsible service owners to map journeys, identify policy and operational barriers, agree improvements and establish accountability across institutional boundaries.
Lead service design standards, accessibility guidance and reusable design resources, embedding research and testing into service development.
Build the human-centred design capability and an approved centre-of-excellence model, supporting journey owners and product teams with research and design expertise.
Partner with the Chief Product Officer to translate end-to-end journey priorities into product roadmaps while retaining visibility of non-digital service steps.
Establish citizen experience measures covering completion, satisfaction, accessibility, waiting time and effort; use segmented evidence to identify exclusion or poor outcomes.
Lead multidisciplinary improvement initiatives with ministries and delivery partners and report progress and unresolved barriers through PDA’s governance arrangements.
Education
Bachelor’s degree in Human-Computer Interaction, Service Design, Design, Psychology, Social Sciences, Public Policy or a related discipline. A relevant master’s degree is preferred. Qualifications must meet PDA’s applicable recognition and equivalence requirements.
Essential experience
At least 15 years of progressively responsible relevant professional experience in citizen or customer experience, service design or human-centred transformation, including senior leadership responsibility.
At least five years building and leading a design centre of excellence, journey management capability or comparable multidisciplinary service improvement function.
Evidence of redesigning complex journeys across organisational boundaries and measuring improvements in service outcomes.
A portfolio or case studies demonstrating research-led design, stakeholder influence and implementation in complex institutional environments.
Desirable experience
Leadership of service design, experience strategy or transformation engagements in consult

Conduct technical and economic assessments of existing refining capacity in Pakistan, identifying modernization needs, infrastructure gaps, and opportunities for efficiency improvement.
Review and advise on refinery configuration, process optimization, product slate diversification, and environmental compliance with national and international standards.
Provide technical input into downstream sector policies, including pricing mechanisms, import/export regulations, blending mandates, and environmental standards (e.g., Euro-V fuels).
Analyze petroleum product supply chains, logistics, storage, and distribution networks to identify bottlenecks, inefficiencies, and investment needs.
Evaluate investment proposals for new refinery projects, brownfield expansions, and associated infrastructure (e.g., pipelines, storage terminals).
Contribute to policy formulation for price deregulation, supply chain resilience, and the introduction of alternative fuels and cleaner energy solutions.
Advise on global and regional petroleum market dynamics, pricing trends, and their implications for domestic pricing strategies and supply security.
Develop financial and technical models to assess the viability of refining and downstream infrastructure projects.
Engage with domestic and international industry stakeholders, including oil marketing companies (OMCs), refinery operators, investors, regulators, and environmental bodies to build consensus and promote sector growth.
Support the design of public-private partnership models, foreign investment attraction strategies, and policy incentives for downstream sector development.
Prepare technical reports, policy briefs, and presentations for senior decision-makers within the Ministry of Energy, Economic Coordination Committee, and Cabinet-level forums.

jobs.title: Financial Analyst (Gas) (SPPS-IV)

Develop and analyze financial models for major gas infrastructure projects, including cross-country pipelines, city gas distribution networks, LNG import terminals, and storage facilities.
Conduct project appraisal, including investment feasibility studies, cost-benefit analysis, and economic impact assessments to inform policy and regulatory decision-making.
Evaluate gas pricing and tariff structures across upstream, midstream, and downstream segments to ensure cost recovery, fair pricing, and affordability for end-users.
Provide financial advisory support for structuring public-private partnerships (PPPs), joint ventures, and other investment models in the gas sector.
Analyze the financial implications of supply diversification strategies, including LNG imports, pipeline interconnectivity, and cross-border gas trade.
Assess the financial sustainability of gas distribution companies (Sui Northern, Sui Southern, etc.) and provide recommendations for reforms or financial strengthening.
Contribute to policy formulation on gas market liberalization, unbundling, and competitive tariff structures while balancing public welfare and investor interests.
Prepare financial impact assessments of regulatory decisions, new project approvals, and market developments for submission to senior management and policy committees.
Monitor international gas market trends, LNG pricing, and regional trade developments to inform domestic pricing strategies and financial planning.
Develop dashboards, reports, and presentations to communicate financial insights to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
